_comment: Grounding / faithfulness. Milestone 3.
THE QUESTION THIS SUITE ASKS: when the model answers, is every factual
claim it makes actually present in the chunks it was given?
HOW IT IS CHECKED WITHOUT AN LLM JUDGE. A judge model is the usual
approach and it is deliberately not used here: the only strong model
wired into this system is the same Groq model that produced the answer,
and a model grading its own output shares its own blind spots.
Instead each case names the SPECIFIC, VERIFIABLE facts involved:
expected_facts   short strings that MUST appear in the answer AND must
be present in the retrieved chunks. Numbers, exact
message text, role names - things with one correct
value that cannot be paraphrased away.
forbidden_facts  plausible-sounding values that are NOT in the corpus.
If one of these shows up in the answer, the model
invented it. This is the hallucination signal.
should_refuse    true when the corpus cannot answer the question at all.
WHAT THIS CANNOT DO: it verifies checkable facts, not full entailment. An
answer can carry a vague unsupported sentence alongside correct numbers
and still score as grounded. That gap is why milestone 4 would need a
judge. See the README.
All facts below were read from eval/corpus_retrieval/*.md by hand.

questions.question: How many digits is the OTP and how long is it valid?
questions.note: two facts, both in 02-otp-delivery.md. Forbidden values are the plausible wrong answers

questions.question: After how many failed login attempts does the account lock, and for how long?
What is the exact error message shown for a mobile number that is too short?
questions.note: exact string match. A paraphrase here is a faithfulness failure even though the meaning is close

questions.question: What are the password requirements?
questions.note: three facts from 04-password-rules.md. 'uppercase' is forbidden because the corpus says number+symbol only

questions.question: How long are audit entries kept and who can read them?
questions.note: 'admin' is forbidden on purpose - it is the intuitive answer and the corpus says auditor role

questions.question: How long can a session stay idle before it expires?
questions.note: 15 and 10 minutes are forbidden because they are real values elsewhere in the corpus (lockout, OTP) - this catches cross-document fact bleed

questions.question: How soon can a user request a new OTP?
What happens to a session token after logout if someone replays it?
questions.note: status code; 403 is the plausible wrong answer

questions.question: What is the minimum contrast ratio required for error text?
questions.note: a number the model could easily substitute from general accessibility knowledge

questions.question: What is the maximum password length allowed?
questions.note: TRAP. The corpus states 'The password field has no maximum length.' A grounded answer says there is no maximum. Inventing a number is the failure. expected_facts is empty because 'no maximum' is phrased too many ways to match on

questions.question: Which encryption algorithm protects stored passwords?
questions.note: not in the corpus at all. The forbidden list is every algorithm a model would reach for from training data

questions.question: How many login attempts per minute are allowed before rate limiting kicks in?
questions.note: sounds adjacent to the lockout rule, which IS in the corpus. Tests whether the model conflates a related fact with the one asked for
